column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my shoulder and said: Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a wayfarer.

And Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both) used to say: When evening comes, do not expect the morning; and when morning comes, do not expect the evening. Take from your health for your illness, and from your life for your death.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.
In the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ taking hold of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar's shoulder there is an alert and an urging to take in what was being imparted to him in that state,
and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar's (may Allah be pleased with them both) reporting that shows how precisely and accurately he retained what he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
since in it he recalls the circumstances in which he heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
His words, “Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a wayfarer”: a stranger is one staying in a land not his own to accomplish some need, ready to leave that land as soon as he is able;

a wayfarer is a traveller who passes through lands without staying in them until his journey ends. The abode of estrangement and of passing through in this hadith is this world, and the journey through it is towards the Hereafter.

That is achieved only by remembering death, keeping one's hopes short and preparing in this world for the Hereafter with righteous deeds, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And take provision, but indeed the best provision is taqwā” [al-Baqarah 2:197].

Al-Bukhārī mentioned in his Ṣaḥīḥ (11/235, with al-Fatḥ) that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “This world has set off, departing, and the Hereafter has set off, approaching, and each has its children. So be children of the Hereafter, and do not be children of this world,

for today there is action and no reckoning, and tomorrow there is reckoning and no action.” The Prophet ﷺ made clear the likeness of this worldly life and its ending, and that it is not an abode of permanence, in his ﷺ words:

“What have I to do with this world? I am in this world only like a rider who took shade under a tree, then went on and left it.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī (2377) and others, who said: “A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.”
His words, “And Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both) used to say: When evening comes, do not expect the morning; and when morning comes, do not expect the evening”:
this shows how quickly the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hastened to carry out the advice of the Messenger ﷺ, and it shows the virtue of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him),
for besides carrying out what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ advised him, he guided others to carry it out.
The meaning is that the Muslim should be expecting death, preparing for it with righteous deeds without laziness or delay, doing righteous deeds in his day as though he would not reach the evening,

and in his night as though he would not reach the morning. In the biography of Manṣūr ibn Zādhān in Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, Hushaym ibn Bashīr al-Wāsiṭī said: “If Manṣūr ibn Zādhān were told that the Angel of Death was at the door, he would have nothing more to add to his deeds.”
His words, “Take from your health for your illness, and from your life for your death”, mean that the Muslim should hasten to righteous deeds while he is able to do them,

in his health, before something comes to hinder him, such as illness or old age; and that he should fill his life with righteous deeds before death takes him by surprise and he moves from the abode of deeds to the abode of recompense.
Encouragement to feel a stranger in this life,
so as to prepare in it with righteous deeds.
A teacher may do something that draws the learner's attention to taking in what is being imparted to him,
since ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my shoulder.”
The Companions hastened to carry out the advice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The virtue of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar in taking up the Prophet's ﷺ advice and urging others to it.
Encouragement to hasten to righteous deeds without laziness or delay.
